subject: Hosting enclave boundary confirmation and list request
messages:
From: Alice Jones <alice.jones@finserv.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: security@finserv.com
Date: 2026-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: exact hosting enclaves in-scope for pen test

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. Our internal assessment team needs a clear list of which hosting enclaves will be considered in scope for the upcoming third-party penetration test before we finalize the scope doc. Specifically, we need to confirm whether the following are in scope under Redwood's responsibilities: 

- Hosted API (multi-tenant, Redwood-managed control plane)
- Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pools with reserved capacity)
- Private/VPC deployments (customer-managed VPCs with Redwood control plane)
- On-prem package (air-gapped customer installations)

Could you provide: 1) which of the above Redwood will cover as part of the standard pen test report, 2) any differences in evidence available between models, and 3) a short list of assets (enclave names or IDs) we should include on our order form?

We are on a tight timeline and would appreciate a response by EOD tomorrow so we can lock scope with our assessor.

Thanks,
Alice Jones
Security Program Manager
FinServ Inc

--

From: priyom.das@redwood.com
To: Alice Jones <alice.jones@finserv.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: exact hosting enclaves in-scope for pen test

Hi Alice,

Thanks — good questions. Short answer up front: we cover Hosted + Dedicated by default for Redwood-managed infrastructure; Private/VPC coverage depends on which plane components you want assessed (Redwood-managed control plane vs customer-managed data plane); on-prem is out-of-scope for our standard test but we can provide guidance and an optional engagement. 

Below is a concise mapping and the artifacts we can provide per hosting mode. I copied Kar thik and Laura for confirmation and artifact handoff. Marcus can flag any infra-only caveats.

Mapping (high-level):
- Hosted API (multi-tenant): in scope for Redwood's pen test. We will include control plane, API endpoints, runtime clusters, and telemetry ingest paths.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): in scope when the capacity is hosted in our DCs; tenant isolation controls, VPC peering endpoints, and GPU-serving nodes are included.
- Private / VPC: split: Redwood-managed control plane components (auth, model registry, routing) are in-scope; customer-managed virtual networks, databases, or on-prem components are out-of-scope unless explicitly contracted.
- On-prem (air-gapped customer): out-of-scope for standard report — we provide a checklist and remote artifact review or a separate on-site assessment for a fee.

Artifacts we can attach: pen-test executive summary, enclave asset list (CSV), control plane topology diagram, and remediation tracker. I've attached a preliminary enclave-asset-list.csv and the pen-test executive summary stub.

If you need the assessor to test a specific customer enclave in Private/VPC, we need an explicit statement of Redwood responsibility and a short access plan (service account + IP allowlist + evidence bucket).

Will follow up tomorrow with more detail from Kar thik on exact endpoints and any exclusions.

Best,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineering (Security Programs)
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: enclave-asset-list.csv, redwood-pen-test-summary-2026-05.pdf

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: Alice Jones <alice.jones@finserv.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-19T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: exact hosting enclaves in-scope for pen test

Hi Alice / team,

Following up with a concrete, itemized inclusion/exclusion list and the exact service endpoints we will include for the standard Redwood pen test (assessor-facing language):

In-scope (standard Redwood assessment):
- Control plane APIs: /v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings (public-facing API gateways behind WAF)
- Runtime clusters: tenant-serving pools for Hosted and Dedicated (GPU nodes, scheduler, KV cache layer)
- Management plane: auth service, model registry, deployment orchestrator (Redwood-managed)
- Telemetry & logging ingestion: collector endpoints and storage buckets we control

Conditional in-scope (requires customer opt-in / access plan):
- Private/VPC: Redwood-managed control plane components (as above) — in-scope. Customer-managed data plane (customer VPC subnets, databases) — OUT unless we have explicit access and assumption of responsibility.
- On-prem: OUT-of-scope unless you request an on-site engagement and share the audited scope statement.

Exclusions (standard):
- Customer-managed data stores, on-prem network appliances, and third-party SaaS hosted inside customer enclaves.

Notes and deliverables:
- We will provide a pen-test executive summary PDF and the full assessor report (redacted for internal findings) once the engagement completes.
- Enclave identifiers: see attached CSV (enclave-asset-list.csv) — please confirm the names to include.
- If you want the assessor to validate a specific Private/VPC data-plane component, please provide: 1) an explicit statement of Redwood responsibility signed by your security owner, 2) temporary service account, 3) IP allowlist window, and 4) S3-style evidence bucket with logs for the testing window.

Planned remediation process: we will open tickets for any critical/high findings and share a remediation tracker with target dates. For Hosted and Dedicated we generally commit to triage within 72 hours and a remediation ETA within 14 days for high severity items. Private/VPC/on-prem timelines depend on customer coordination.

Happy to hop on a short call if that helps finalize scope.

Thanks,
Kar thik Iyer
Principal Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

--
